scale.formula: score = 1 + 2 × (average driver rating − 1), where Low = 1, Medium = 2, High = 3. An average of 1.0 maps to 1, 2.0 to 3, 3.0 to 5.
scale.rounding: Whole numbers only. A raw score that lands on a half (e.g. 2.5) rounds UP, toward the stronger force — a deliberately conservative bias for anyone deciding whether to enter or invest. Any raw score with a fractional part between .33 and .67 is flagged as a tension and named in the rationale.
scale.driverRule: Each driver is rated from the net direction of its cited facts: more facts that raise the force than lower it → High; balanced or only mixed facts → Medium; more that lower it → Low. A driver with no cited facts is left unrated and drops out of the average.

confidence.Medium: 3 cited facts, or 4+ from fewer than 3 documents
confidence.Low: fewer than 3 cited facts — the score is shown but should not be relied on

forces.name: Threat of new entrants
forces.question: How easily could a new competitor get in and take profit?

drivers.name: Capital requirements
drivers.note: Big entry costs are a barrier, so evidence of them LOWERS the threat.

drivers.name: Access to talent & distribution
drivers.note: Locked-up distribution, talent or channels LOWER the threat.

drivers.name: Incumbent retaliation & regulation
drivers.note: Expected retaliation or regulatory hurdles LOWER the threat.

drivers.name: Credible recent entrants
drivers.note: Recent, funded entrants that stuck RAISE the threat.

forces.name: Bargaining power of suppliers
forces.question: Can the providers of key inputs (talent, materials, IP) capture the profit?

drivers.name: Suppliers' outside options
drivers.note: If suppliers can easily sell elsewhere, their power RISES; if those options collapse, it falls.

forces.name: Bargaining power of buyers
forces.question: Can customers (here: broadcasters, sponsors, fans) push prices down?

drivers.name: Buyer switching costs & lock-in
drivers.note: Long contracts and high switching costs LOWER buyer power until renewal.

drivers.name: Buyers' alternatives
drivers.note: When buyers have no comparable product to switch to, their power FALLS.

forces.name: Threat of substitutes
forces.question: Can a different product meet the same need (here: fans' time, sponsors' dollars)?

drivers.name: Customer switching costs & loyalty
drivers.note: Habit, loyalty and deeper engagement LOWER the substitute threat.

forces.name: Rivalry among existing competitors
forces.question: How hard do current competitors fight over the same profit pool?

drivers.name: Industry growth
drivers.note: Fast growth LOWERS rivalry (everyone can win); slow or declining growth raises it.

drivers.name: Fixed costs, exit barriers & spending wars
Product differentiation
drivers.note: Clear differentiation LOWERS rivalry; commodity products raise it.
